Deeptech energy startup Adiabatic Technologies has raised ₹8.3 crore in a seed funding round led by Malpani Ventures and Avinya Ventures, with participation from Appreciate Capital, DeVC, Operators Studio, and the UPES Incubator.

The Ahilyanagar and Pune-based startup will use the funding to expand its manufacturing capacity to 100 MWh annually, accelerate product development, and grow its engineering team. It is also expanding deployments across robotics, drones, defence, electric mobility, marine, agri-equipment, and industrial energy storage.

Founded in 2022, Adiabatic has deployed over 20,000 battery systems with 25+ OEMs, focusing on in-house battery design and proprietary battery management systems (BMS) for high-performance, mission-critical applications.

Chennai-based Inventus Battery Energy Technologies is spearheading the solid-state battery race in India, aiming for commercialisation by 2026.   
  
These advanced batteries promise faster charging, higher energy density, and enhanced safety—ideal for EVs, renewable energy systems, and everyday devices.  
  
With a "plug-and-play" technology compatible with existing Li-ion manufacturing setups, Inventus is filling India's battery tech gap. The startup focuses on innovation, offering solutions like LFP and NMC batteries, raw material manufacturing, and battery recycling for a sustainable future.

These two founders, Nimisha Varma and Naveen Suman, are rethinking what a battery can be made from. Their startup, Aloe E-Cell, is building plant-powered batteries using aloe vera, while also finding a way to turn used batteries into fertilizer.
A fascinating example of how young founders are solving a very real problem, India’s growing battery waste, with an unexpectedly simple idea.
